description: DSEQ PARSE IS WRONG against real CLI output. `provider-services tx deployment create -o json` returns a Cosmos SDK TxResponse, NOT an object with a top-level `dseq` field. The dseq is emitted as a tx EVENT ATTRIBUTE of the form {"key":"dseq","value":"<n>"} nested under .logs[].events[].attributes[] (or .events[] on newer CLIs). The script's `jq -r '.. | .dseq? // empty' | head -1` recurses the whole document looking for an object KEY literally named `dseq`. In real output there is no such key whose value is the dseq number — `dseq` only ever appears as the VALUE of a `key` attribute. Therefore on a REAL successful broadcast the jq yields empty -> the script hits line 72 and fail-closes with 'no dseq — deployment tx failed' even though the deployment succeeded. The deploy will NEVER work on testnet/mainnet. This is the dimension-3 highest-risk defect and it is masked by the fake.

evidence.snippet: DSEQ="$("$PS" tx deployment create "$SDL_FILE" --from "$AKASH_KEY_NAME" -y -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.. | .dseq? // empty' | head -1)"

correctFix: Parse the dseq from the tx event attributes, e.g.: `jq -r '[..|.attributes? // empty]|flatten|map(select(.key=="dseq"))|.[0].value // empty'`, or more robustly query it back: after broadcast, `provider-services query deployment list --owner $ADDR -o json | jq -r '.deployments[-1].deployment.deployment_id.dseq'` (or filter by tx height). Do NOT rely on a top-level `.dseq`. Also note `2>/dev/null` swallows the broadcast error, compounding the silent failure.
